profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility is located at 501 West 2nd Avenue, Spokane, WA 99201; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites.

Eastern Washington's Spokane County is emerging as a new data center growth area distinct from the Columbia Basin hydro hub around Quincy and Wenatchee that hosts other operators tracked in this registry. Avista Utilities, Spokane's primary electric provider, filed a nonbinding memorandum of understanding with the SEC on May 29, 2026 to supply an unnamed large customer with 125 megawatts starting in 2029, scaling to as much as 500 megawatts by 2032, a figure equal to about 16% of Avista's current roughly 3,000-megawatt system peak capacity; the deal still requires formal review by the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission, including engineering studies and reliability protections, before it can proceed.

Spokane's emerging data center interest, anchored by Avista's 2026 large-load agreement, is a separate development from the decades-old Columbia Basin hydro cluster around Quincy and Wenatchee that hosts several other operators tracked in this registry, reflecting Eastern Washington's broader push to diversify beyond its traditional agricultural and hydro-power economy.

reading.body:
This facility in Spokane is attributed to Lumen Technologies but publishes no power capacity figure. Lumen divested its data center business to Cyxtera Technologies in 2017, retaining a stake, and whether this specific building was part of that sale or remains on Lumen's books cannot be determined from published sources.

Washington state has 46 mapped data center facilities, of which only two publish power capacity. This Spokane location ranks third by published megawatts in the state, but that ranking reflects the absence of published data rather than a known power figure. The two facilities with published capacity in Washington total 60 MW.

Without a published power specification, this campus cannot be assessed for its role in AI infrastructure scaling. No dedicated product page, facility specification, or capacity commitment is available. Whether Lumen operates this address as active colocation infrastructure, what tenants it hosts, what power it draws, or what its buildout roadmap might be remains unknown.
